t.7.37.1: Then Rāma, having reflected, embraced his friend Pratardana, the lord of Kāśi, who feared nothing from any quarter, and spoke these words.
t.7.37.2: Affection has been shown by you, and the highest friendship has been shown; and effort has been made, O king, by Bharata together with you.
t.7.37.3: Therefore, go today, sir, to Vārāṇasī, the city of the Kāśīs, a delightful city protected by you, with fine ramparts and beautiful gateways.
t.7.37.4: Having said this much, the righteous-souled Kākutstha rose from his excellent seat and embraced him tightly, clasped close to his breast.
t.7.37.5: Having dismissed that friend of his, Rāghava, smiling, spoke words of sweet syllables to the kings of the earth who had come to him.
t.7.37.6: Your contentment is undisturbed, guarded by your splendour; your righteousness is ever steadfast, and truth is always yours.
t.7.37.7: Through the might and the splendour of you great-souled ones, the wicked-souled and evil-minded Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, has been slain.
t.7.37.8: I was a mere instrument there; it was by your valour that Rāvaṇa was slain in battle together with his hosts, his sons and his kinsmen.
t.7.37.9: And you were brought here by the great-souled Bharata, who had heard that the daughter of King Janaka had been carried off in the forest.
t.7.37.10: Indeed, a very long time has passed for all these great-souled kings who stand ready; let your mind now be inclined toward their departure.
t.7.37.11: And the kings, filled with great joy, replied to him: "By good fortune you are victorious, O Rāma, and your kingdom too is firmly established."
t.7.37.12: By good fortune Sītā has been brought back, and by good fortune the enemy has been defeated. This is our highest desire, and this is our supreme glory.
t.7.37.13: That we behold you victorious, Rāma, with your enemies slain, and that you, Kākutstha, praise us, this is indeed fitting.
t.7.37.14: Only those who are themselves worthy of praise know how to speak praise such as this. We take our leave and shall depart; you will always dwell in our hearts. And may your affection for us remain forever, O great king.
